question: A team reviews SQL Server 2025 external-model definitions for an AI application. It proposes using the same model-object mechanism for embeddings and chat-answer generation. Under the documented MODEL_TYPE contract, which conclusion is supported? Consider the local ONNX Runtime alternative in its explicitly documented Preview scope; no model invocation is being performed.

answerChoices.text: Declare MODEL_TYPE = CHAT_COMPLETIONS to register the chat-generation purpose.
Keep MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS and change API_FORMAT to Azure OpenAI to make it a chat-generation object.
Keep MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS and select the local ONNX Runtime Preview format to make it a chat-generation object.
Treat the documented external-model type as embedding-only; chat generation needs a separately documented interface outside this model-object contract.

explanation: The current reference lists EMBEDDINGS as the accepted MODEL_TYPE. Changing the provider format or selecting local ONNX does not introduce a chat-generation model type.
deepExplanation: API_FORMAT identifies the provider's message format, while MODEL_TYPE identifies the operation's purpose. The local ONNX example retains MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS and has explicit developer Preview status. This question evaluates those model-definition fields only; it does not select, invoke or make lifecycle claims about a separate chat transport.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: CHAT_COMPLETIONS is not an accepted MODEL_TYPE in the cited current definition.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: Azure OpenAI is an accepted API_FORMAT, but selecting it does not change the EMBEDDINGS model type into chat generation.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: The documented local ONNX Preview definition also uses EMBEDDINGS; its execution location does not create a different model type.
